normalized.prelim_summary: This 2017 Lexus GX460 Premium has high mileage but a documented dealer service history and clean Carfax title. It has been modified with a leveling kit, new grille, and ceramic coating, with the desirable bench third-row seat. Priced at $21,000 by a private seller in Fort Worth, TX.

documentation.rationale: Partial. A full dealer-service history is claimed and said to be checkable online, and a partial invoice photo for the suspension work is shown. However, there is no VIN, no attached Carfax, no service records, and no evidence on the GX at-risk items (AI pump, KDSS, valley plate, frame). Both identity and maintenance halves are thin.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight, glossy paint, intact trim, stock wheels on decent Michelins and a clean interior with only light driver-seat soiling. The suspension is freshly installed with an alignment. Mechanical condition at 173k is unproven: no scan, no underside photos, and no fluid or cooling evidence.

price_value.rationale: The $21,000 ask sits near the top of the $13,710–$21,554 fair-value range and well above the $16,301 mid. A comparable 2017 Premium with 165,800 miles sold for $17,750. The lift and grille do not add comparable value.

mission_fit.rationale: A body-on-frame V8 with full-time 4WD, low range, roof rails and a mild quality level is real capability the RX 350 lacks, and it suits a rooftop tent or sleeping platform. It is within the budget band. Mileage is high but it is a Lexus, and the mild lift is only a small positive.

logistics.rationale: Fort Worth is far from Carmel, but PPI options there are plentiful, and the drive home is straightforward. PPI access has not been confirmed by the seller. CA out-of-state registration and smog should be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: This is an attractive dark blue over tan Premium with a tasteful Eibach level. The grille swap is a cosmetic update and not an original feature. Otherwise it is a fairly typical example.

ppi_focus: Full OBD scan including pending and history codes, with specific attention to P2440/P2442/P2445 and readiness monitors
KDSS cylinders, accumulators and lines for leaks; check level stance and drop-bracket install quality
Lift install: CV boot angles and condition, track bar bracket welds/bolts, sway bar end links, alignment within spec
Valley-plate coolant seepage at the rear of the engine and timing-cover oil seepage
Frame rails, crossmembers and rear hitch area for rust, towing wear and impact damage
Transmission, transfer case and differential fluid condition, and the transfer case actuator/4LO engagement
Stock rear shocks and bushings at 173k and the front control arm bushings
Remote-start wiring quality and battery drain
Tire date codes and even wear after the alignment
Paint-depth readings for undisclosed bodywork, since a ceramic coat can hide refinish
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a VIN with a clean Carfax and full Sewell dealer records showing on-time fluids, plugs and no AI-pump faults.
Up: a clean PPI with no codes, a dry KDSS, a dry valley plate and a solid frame.
Up: a price negotiated toward the $16k–18k comps.
Down: AI-pump codes or history of repeated AI repairs, KDSS leaks, or valley-plate coolant seepage.
Down: refusal to provide the VIN or allow a PPI, or evidence of heavy towing or an undisclosed accident.
evidence.mission_note: A GX460 with a mild quality level supplies real body-on-frame, low-range and rooftop-tent capability the RX 350 does not, so it fits the utility_capability branch. Its overlap with the household RX means the case rests on that capability plus verified condition, not on price.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2017 GX460 Premium at 173,333 miles in Fort Worth with a claimed clean Carfax title and claimed Sewell Lexus dealer service since new. None of that is documented here: no VIN, no report and no service records are provided. The photos show a cosmetically clean dark-blue/tan example on stock wheels and Michelins, with light driver-seat soiling and a fitted trailer hitch receiver. A partial, undated invoice supports the July Eibach 2.5" level, KDSS/sway bar drop mounts, track bar bracket and alignment. The model's key questions remain open: secondary air injection history, KDSS condition after the lift, valley-plate coolant seepage and frame condition. 'No check engine lights' is a seller sentence, not a scan. The $21,000 ask sits near the top of the $13,710–$21,554 fair-value range, against a $16,301 mid and a $17,750 sale of a similar-mileage 2017 Premium.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN and confirmation that a PPI at a Fort Worth Lexus dealer or independent shop is allowed, then pull the Carfax and Lexus service history before discussing price.
